text:
The Four Friends and the Hidden Laws of Amun
Thebes, 1350 BC
Chapter One: The Golden Monkey
On a sunny morning in Thebes, the temple of Amun was bustling with new life. Sunbeams
sneaked between the pillars of Osiris, leaving golden patches on the marble floor. Suddenly,
a loud scream cut through the silence.
"The necklace! Catch him!"
High Priest Paser was running after a small monkey with copper-red fur, panting and
shouting. The monkey held a golden ankh necklace between its teeth, shining like a piece
of the sun.
Nebufra, the strongest boy in his village, was standing at the temple gate practising
jumps. He did not hesitate. He ran after the monkey, counting the steps in his head:
If I run at a speed of 3 metres per second, how far will I go after 10 seconds?

But the
monkey was faster than he expected.
The monkey jumped onto the shoulder of Senmuti, a thin, long-necked boy who was
leaning over a limestone tablet copying hieroglyphic texts. Senmuti almost fell from
surprise. He stared at his leather bag full of papyrus tablets and said to himself:

The
bag's mass is 80 kilograms, and gravity is 10, what is its weight?

But the monkey gave
him no time.
The monkey dashed like lightning to Hor-Amun, a dark-skinned wrestler with sharp eyes
who was practising his moves in a corner of the temple. Hor-Amun lunged to catch the
monkey, thinking of the laws of combat:

My mass is 15 kilograms and my speed is 20
metres per second, what is my momentum?

Yet the monkey twisted away like a snake.
At the other end of the courtyard, Titi was sitting quietly, eating a date and enjoying the
sun. He saw the monkey approaching, so he grabbed the fishing net he had prepared for
a trip to the Nile after prayers. He threw the net in a smooth circular motion.
In one instant everyone was tangled together: the monkey, Nebufra, Senmuti, Hor-Amun,
and Titi. They rolled on the floor like a single ball of arms, legs, shouts and laughter.
High Priest Paser stood over them, panting from the chase, and looked at the tangled
heap. He wiped his sweat with his robe and then said:

Today's temperature is 38 °C.
What is it in Fahrenheit?

Everyone was silent. No one knew the answer.
"Well," Paser said with a smile that was not completely kind, "you will work for me
cleaning the rear chapel for one week. Start now."
That was the beginning of a friendship that lasted for years. Every day of their punishment
they discovered something new about the temple and about each other. When the week
ended, they could no longer imagine their lives without this strange friendship.
Chapter Two: The Race of the Seven Pillars
After a full year of daily meetings under the temple colonnades, Nebufra decided that the
time had come to determine who was the strongest among them. He challenged them to a
race around the temple seven times. The winner would receive the title "Lion of Amun",
and the losers would offer him two honey cakes.
They stood at the first pylon, hearts beating with excitement. Just before the start signal,
Emma, the temple guard's daughter, passed by on her wooden bicycle. She was speeding
and then braked suddenly. Senmuti shouted:

Her speed is 7 metres per second, she
stops in 5 seconds, what is her acceleration?

No one waited for an answer. Nebufra let out a yell and they all rushed among the huge
columns.
Nebufra was in front, but he found a huge stone block blocking his way. The priests had
placed it there to prevent worshippers from approaching a renovation area. Nebufra did
not hesitate; he pushed the block.

How much work does he do if he pushes with a
force of 8 N over a distance of 5 m?

Sofia exerts a force of 50 N on an arm of length 3 m.
What is her torque?

She can lift a weight bigger than herself!
They reached the western colonnade where a huge wooden box stood. The air was hot and
sweat poured from their brows. Hor-Amun read the numbers carved on the wall beside
the box and said:

The normal force is 70 N, the coefficient of friction is 0.1. What is
the friction force we must overcome?

Push!
They pushed together and got past it.
They climbed the back stairs of the temple and reached the roof where the huge water
jars for ablution were kept. Titi lifted a full jar to a height of 3 m and poured it over his
head in triumph. He shouted:

The jar's mass is 30 kg, what gravitational potential
energy did it gain?

They went down to the tug-of-war courtyard. Two teams were competing. Voices were
loud, ropes were tight. Senmuti asked while panting:

If the right team pulls with
30 N and the left team pulls with 35 N, what is the net force and which way does the flag
move?

Nebufra jumped over an old war chariot displayed as a souvenir. He looked at the starting
and ending marks of the chariot: it started at 20 m and ended at 30 m. He said:

What
is the displacement of this chariot during its imaginary journey?

At the Nile gate they saw a racing chariot being tested. It accelerated from rest to a
speed of 9 m/s in 10 s. Hor-Amun cried out:
What is its acceleration?

Just as Nebufra was about to reach the finish line, a stray cat – the same one they secretly
fed – crossed his path. Nebufra stumbled and fell. Titi laughed and said:

The cat
did 50 J of work over a distance of 5 m. What is the cat's force?

It is stronger than we
think!
The race ended with Senmuti winning by accident.
They sat on the temple roof to rest, breathing the sweet Nile breeze. A small child was
sliding down a stone slope nearby. Titi said:

The work done on the child is 150 J,
and its potential energy changed by 90 J. How much did its kinetic energy change?

That
is why he is so fast.
In the lower colonnade they saw a bowling ball rolling slowly. Nebufra said:

Its
mass is 15 kg and its speed is 20 m/s. What is its momentum?

This ball will knock down
everything in its way.
The temple guard, a muscular man who practised karate, passed by them. They saw him
strike a wooden board with a force of 60 N, but the blow lasted only 0.4 s. They heard the
board crack. Senmuti said:
What impulse did the guard deliver to the board?

A small elephant came to drink from the temple's sacred pool. Its steps were heavy.
Hor-Amun said:

One foot of this elephant exerts a force of 225 N over an area of 5 m².
What pressure does it produce?

No wonder the ground trembles.
On their way home they saw a cheetah chasing a gazelle in the desert. The cheetah
covered 60 m in only 3 s. Titi shouted:
What is the cheetah's speed?

Faster than any
human without doubt.
A soldier launched a model rocket to celebrate the festival of Amun. The rocket reached a
speed of 20 m/s after 10 s from launch. Nebufra said:
What is the rocket's acceleration?

On top of a small obelisk reserved for children, a boy played with a ball. The ball fell
from his hand, and its kinetic energy changed by 180 J. Senmuti said:

How much did
its potential energy change?
They looked at a distant hill that they planned to explore one day. Hor-Amun said:

The hill's vertical height is 175 units, and its horizontal distance is 500 units. What is
the tangent of its slope angle?

In a small field behind the temple, a guard caught a fast baseball with his hand. Its kinetic
energy changed by –605 J. Titi said:
How much did its potential energy change?

It
all went into the guard's glove and his poor hand.
Chapter Three: The Serpent's Dungeon
Days later, High Priest Paser gave them a new task: clean the old dungeon under the
temple. He said it had not been opened for years, and spiders and reptiles might have
accumulated there.
They descended the dark spiral staircase, each carrying a torch of waxed papyrus. The
humidity was high, the air heavy with the smell of earth and mould. Suddenly they heard
a hiss. Then they saw it: a huge serpent, its body as thick as a man's forearm, emerging
from a broken stone sarcophagus.
The serpent fled into a side passage, and the four friends bravely followed it.
They reached a strange room they had never seen before: the room of pendulums. A
huge grandfather clock stood there, its wooden pendulum swinging very slowly. Senmuti
noticed that the pendulum completes one full swing every 5 s. He said:

What is the
frequency of this pendulum?

Beside the clock there was a small, strange pendulum labelled with special units: gravita-
tional acceleration g = 1, string length L = 1. Hor-Amun said:

What is the angular
frequency of this pendulum?

It looks like the work of a mad priest.
The ground suddenly shook. A collapse had occurred in a distant old part of the temple.
The friends felt a wave travelling through the earth. They measured its frequency as 20 Hz
and its wavelength as 4 m. Nebufra shouted:
What is the speed of this wave?

If it
were water, we would drown.
In a corner of the room they found a large bronze spring that was holding a heavy stone
door shut. They tried to remove it, but it was very stiff. They read strange numbers on
it: period T = 1 and spring constant k = 1 (in special units). Titi said:

What is the
speed of this spring?

I don't understand these units.
Finally they managed to catch the serpent using ropes and daggers. They carried it out
of the dungeon and threw it into a dry well behind the temple.
They came out into the outer courtyard exhausted. The priests were testing a new
loudspeaker with a power of 30 W. The sound filled the yard. Senmuti said:

If the
sound spreads over an area of 5 m², what is its intensity?

They crossed the metal bridge that connected the temple to the grain stores. The bridge
was hot under their feet. Hor-Amun said:

The initial length of the bridge is 6 units,
its linear expansion coefficient is 4, and the temperature rises by 150degrees. How much
does it lengthen?
In High Priest Paser's laboratory they saw a huge mercury thermometer. Nebufra said:

Its initial volume is 1, its volume expansion coefficient is 7, and the temperature rises
by 5degrees. How much does the mercury's volume change?

They entered the food storage room. A large pot of soup was boiling over a gentle fire.
Titi asked:

If the pot's heat capacity is 30 and it is heated by 5degrees, how much
heat is added?

While they were eating the soup, Senmuti noticed a ray of light entering through a small
hole in the ceiling. The ray bent as it passed through the soup's surface. He said:

The speed of light in vacuum is 30 units, and in the soup it is 15 units. What is the
refractive index of the soup?

Maybe this is the secret of its delicious taste.
The friends looked into a concave mirror hanging on the temple wall. It was used to
ignite offerings by concentrating sunlight. Hor-Amun said:

Its focal length is 90
units. What is its radius of curvature?
They tried a small telescope that once belonged to an old astronomer-priest. Nebufra said:

The objective lens value is +50, the eyepiece value is 5. What is the magnification
ratio?

Chapter Four: The Cave of Electrical Secrets
At the end of the secret passage they had discovered behind the western altar, the friends
found a stone door decorated with strange carvings they had never seen before. They
pushed it with difficulty, and a wide room opened before them, illuminated by a faint
glow from crystals set into the walls. It was the ancient room of electricity – or as the old
priest Thothi called it, "Amun's hidden laboratory."
The first thing that caught their attention was a huge circular coil of red copper. Beside
it a clay tablet was inscribed in hieroglyphics: number of turns N = 30, current I = 5 A,
radius r = 30cm. Nebufra said:
What is the magnetic field at the centre of this coil?

On the cave wall they found a charged metal plate. The charge was evenly distributed
on its surface. They read: total charge Q = 400 units, area A = 5 m². Senmuti said:
What is the surface charge density?

Next to the plate there was a long wire stretching from one wall to another. Hor-Amun
said:

The charge on this wire is 500 units, and its length is 10 units. What is the
linear charge density?

Old Thothi entered behind them, carrying a small device. He passed an electric field of
magnitude 5 through a loop of area 30. Titi said:

What is the electric flux through
this loop?

Then they applied Gauss's law. Thothi placed a charge of 505 inside a closed copper
surface and asked them to calculate the flux. Nebufra said:

The permittivity of free
space is 5 units. What is the electric flux?

In a corner of the cave they found an old capacitor. They read on it: it stores a charge of
80 C at a voltage of 4 V. Senmuti said:
What is the capacitance of this capacitor?

Beside it, three small capacitors were connected in parallel: 10 F, 20 F, 10 F. Hor-Amun
said:
What is the equivalent capacitance of this parallel combination?
The same three capacitors were also connected in series in another circuit. Titi said:
What is the equivalent capacitance in series?

Nearby there was a tablet describing a lightning bolt. It read: this lightning bolt transfers
a charge of 5 C through a potential difference of 35 V. Nebufra said:

How much work
does the lightning bolt do?

Another capacitor was connected to a battery. Its initial voltage was 600 V. Then they
inserted an ivory slab (a dielectric) between its plates, with a dielectric constant k = 3.
Senmuti said:
What is the new voltage after inserting the dielectric?

At the end of the cave there was a small motor turning quietly. They measured its output
power as 55 and its input power as 60. Hor-Amun said:

What is the efficiency of this
motor as a percentage?

The last thing they saw was a tiny lamp that still glowed faintly after thousands of years.
They read on its base: current I = 5 A, voltage V = 10 V. Titi smiled and said:

What
is the power of this amazing lamp?

Old Thothi smiled. He said: "I have your answers, but I will not give them to you today.
Search for them yourselves in the books of wisdom."
The friends left the cave, their minds full of questions. They sat under the statue of
Thoth, god of knowledge and calculation, and decided they would learn all these laws
– not because the priest asked them to, but because they understood that the whole
universe is written in the language of numbers.
From that day on, their visits to the cave became a secret of their friendship. Whenever
they faced a new question, they returned to the cave to discover more.
Thus lived the four friends – Nebufra the strong, Senmuti the wise, Hor-Amun the brave,
and Titi the skilful – in Thebes during the era of the New Kingdom, learning the laws of
nature while playing among the colonnades of the temple of Amun.
